text: Fill in the missing value or term for each statement about obesity and the metabolic syndrome in Indian practice.
questions: For Asian Indians, the BMI threshold for overweight is *23:Indian obesity begins at BMI 25, not the international 30.* kg per m squared, lower than the international cut-off.
Central obesity in Indian men is defined as a waist circumference of *90:The threshold for Indian women is 80 cm.* cm or more.
Enlarged visceral adipocytes secrete less *adiponectin:This is the one protective adipokine that falls as visceral fat increases.* and more TNF-alpha and IL-6, promoting insulin resistance.

The metabolic syndrome is diagnosed when any *three/3:Any combination of that many out of five criteria qualifies.* of five criteria are present: central obesity, raised triglycerides, low HDL, raised blood pressure and raised fasting glucose.

The core biochemical defect linking visceral obesity to the metabolic syndrome is *insulin resistance:Free fatty acids impair insulin signalling in liver and muscle.*, driven by portal free fatty acids from visceral fat.

overallFeedback.feedback: Asian Indians develop metabolic complications at lower BMI and waist circumference than Western populations because of higher visceral fat at any given BMI (the 'thin-fat' phenotype); the metabolic syndrome criteria capture the cluster of abnormalities driven by visceral-fat-induced insulin resistance.
